offences.quote: Failing to follow specific instructions relating to the use of AI within the assessment brief, except for documented inclusive support adjustments.
Failing to acknowledge/reference any permitted use of AI within an assessment.
Generating an assessment in its entirety and submitting it as the student’s own work.
Attempting to use AI to humanise or attempt to hide the use of AI so that the submitted assessment does not reflect the student’s own understandings, thoughts or ideas.
Commissioning of Assessed Work occurs where a student commissions a third party to complete all or part of an assessed piece of work and then submits it as their own.
Plagiarism occurs where a student copies words or ideas from another person and presents those words or ideas as their own in an assessment without properly acknowledging and citing the source(s).
Fabrication occurs where a student creates data, results or other outputs and presents them as if they were real.
use of any information, communication, technology device e.g. mobile phone, watch or calculator during an examination, unless expressly permitted by the examination regulations

liability.quote: It is not necessary for intent to be proven in determining whether an offence of academic misconduct has occurred.
Category 4 will normally be defined as gross academic misconduct where a clear intent to deceive and gain an unfair academic advantage can be established.
It is normally the result of a failure to understand the required protocols and is most likely to occur at an early stage in the course

detection.quote: Turnitin UK generates an Originality Report to facilitate the identification of potential plagiarism cases.

interpreting detection software reports, where the substance of the copied material will be considered as well as the quantity, and there is no percentage threshold for an investigation to be initiated
Academic judgment will be applied based on the evidence that is available when identifying suspected cases of academic misconduct.

Where it is suspected that a student has submitted work that has not been written by them, the student may be asked questions about the work during an interview with the Academic Integrity Officer or Academic Misconduct Committee
Students must retain draft copies of work used in the preparation of final submissions to help prove the work is their own, if challenged.

process.quote: the student will be invited to a meeting with a member of staff (usually the module leader) who will explain the nature of the concern.
should report the case to the relevant Academic Integrity Lead and provide any evidence to support the allegation.
The Academic Integrity Lead will review the evidence and may conduct an initial investigation which may involve interviewing the student.
The student will be notified of the allegation against them and will be asked to submit a written response
The student will be invited to a hearing with the Academic Misconduct Committee.
If the student does not attend without good cause, a decision may be made in their absence and a penalty may be imposed
At all stages of this Policy, a student is entitled to be accompanied by a person of their choosing, who may be from the Students’ Union Advice and Representation Centre.
The student may submit an appeal within 10 working days of the official notification of the outcome of a decision by the Academic Integrity Lead or the Academic Misconduct Committee
The University will aim to deal with suspected cases of academic misconduct within 25 working days from the date when the marks are released.
The standard of proof will be the civil standard of proof which means that ‘on a balance of probabilities’ the facts of the allegation are more likely than not to have happened.

outcomes.quote: This will be a formative learning opportunity for the student who will be given advice and will be referred to relevant support and educational opportunities regarding good academic practice.
A written warning setting out the consequences of further academic misconduct and a referral to learning opportunities regarding good academic practice.
the mark for the element of assessment may be reduced (by 10% of the maximum mark) to reflect the failure to address the assessment criteria regarding referencing.
A mark of 0% for the element of assessment which must be resubmitted where permitted*, to the required standard.
The mark for the element of assessment following resubmission will be capped at the minimum pass mark.
A mark of 0% for the module with no opportunity for re-assessment.
Students can be excluded from the University for very serious or repeat offences.
the Assessment Board may recommend that the award be rescinded in accordance with the Academic Regulations.
Category 3 academic misconduct will normally be defined as a repeat offence of academic misconduct in any form
The penalties for academic misconduct will be determined based on:

definitions.quote: Academic misconduct is defined as any action or attempted action by a student which gives or has the potential to give an unfair advantage in an assessment
Academic misconduct will occur where a student uses technological aids and/or Artificial Intelligence (AI) to gain an unfair advantage in meeting the assessment learning outcomes.
Plagiarism occurs where a student copies words or ideas from another person and presents those words or ideas as their own in an assessment without properly acknowledging and citing the source(s).
Collusion is an attempt to deceive the examiners by disguising the true authorship of an assessed piece of work in full or in part.
Commissioning of Assessed Work occurs where a student commissions a third party to complete all or part of an assessed piece of work and then submits it as their own.
Poor academic practice falls short of academic misconduct and normally occurs where a student has attempted but failed to adopt good academic practice.
